title: Zerocoin
brief: Ian Miers, Christina Garman, Matthew Green and Aviel Rubin at Johns Hopkins show how to bolt anonymous coins onto Bitcoin using zero-knowledge proofs. It works, but coins come in fixed denominations and the proofs are bulky.
notes: Zerocoin: Anonymous Distributed E-Cash from Bitcoin, IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy, 2013
The first serious design for unlinkable payments on a public chain. Its limits set the problem the next paper solved.

title: Zerocash
brief: Seven researchers replace Zerocoin's proofs with zk-SNARKs. Payments now hide sender, receiver and amount, transactions are under 1 kB and verify in under 6 ms. This is the protocol Zcash ships.
notes: Zerocash: Decentralized Anonymous Payments from Bitcoin, IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy, 2014

title: The Ceremony
brief: Six people in six places jointly generate Zcash's zk-SNARK parameters. As long as one of them destroyed their share of the secret, nobody can forge coins. Laptops were wiped and hardware destroyed.
people: John Dobbertin: revealed in 2022 to be Edward Snowden
notes: The Sprout proving and verifying keys. The toxic waste behind them had to be destroyed: the trusted setup Halo later removed.

title: Genesis
brief: Zcash mainnet launches. Shielded value lives in the Sprout pool; blocks every 150 seconds; Equihash proof of work; a 21 million cap with a slow start over the first 20,000 blocks.
people: Zooko Wilcox: CEO, Zerocoin Electric Coin Company
notes: Founders' Reward: 20% of the block subsidy for the first four years
Equihash, by Alex Biryukov and Dmitry Khovratovich
Slow start: rewards ramped up over the first 20,000 blocks

title: Sapling
brief: Sapling activated at 02:15 UTC (28 October US time). It cut shielded proving to seconds and about 40 MB of memory with Groth16, separated proving from spend authority, and added full viewing keys. ZIPs: 205 (deployment) and 243; it also closed CVE-2019-7167.
people: Sean Bowe: BLS12-381, Jubjub, the MPC
Ariel Gabizon: MPC design, with Bowe and Ian Miers
notes: A new shielded pool, Sapling, with zs1 addresses
Viewing keys that work in practice
New parameters from Powers of Tau plus a Sapling MPC, with many participants instead of six

title: Halo
brief: Sean Bowe, Jack Grigg and Daira Hopwood publish recursive proof composition without a trusted setup. The ceremonies are no longer needed. It becomes Halo 2, and Halo 2 becomes Orchard.
notes: Recursive Proof Composition without a Trusted Setup, 2019

title: NU5 / Orchard
brief: NU5 activated at 17:50 UTC, adding the Orchard pool on Halo 2 with no trusted setup, Unified Addresses, v5 transactions and non-malleable txids. ZIPs: 252 (deployment), 224, 225, 216, 239, 244 and 316.
people: Daira Hopwood, Sean Bowe, Jack Grigg: Halo 2 and Orchard
notes: Halo 2 proofs on the Pallas and Vesta curves

title: NU6 + 2nd halving
brief: NU6 activated with the second halving and replaced the ZIP 1014 dev fund: 8% to Zcash Community Grants and 12% to an in-protocol lockbox. It also required coinbase to claim the full subsidy plus fees. ZIPs: 253 (deployment), 236, 1015, 2001.
notes: Zcash Community Grants: 8% of the subsidy

title: NU6.3 / Ironwood
brief: NU6.3 created the Ironwood shielded pool with quantum-recoverable notes (ZIP 2005) and v6 transactions (ZIP 229). It restricted Orchard so no new value can enter, and coins leaving Orchard pass a turnstile so supply integrity can be checked. Deployment ZIP 258 (branch ID 0x37A5165B), also ZIP 2006, with wallet ZIPs 318 and 326.

title: Chaum blind signatures
brief: David Chaum's paper "Blind Signatures for Untraceable Payments" appeared in Advances in Cryptology, the CRYPTO '82 proceedings, published 1983 (pp. 199-203). It introduced blind signatures, the basis for anonymous digital cash and a direct ancestor of the privacy goals behind Zcash.

title: Zero-knowledge proofs
brief: Shafi Goldwasser, Silvio Micali and Charles Rackoff presented "The Knowledge Complexity of Interactive Proof-Systems" at STOC '85 in Providence, Rhode Island. The paper defined zero-knowledge proofs, the concept every Zcash shielded transaction relies on.

title: Pinocchio
brief: Bryan Parno, Craig Gentry, Jon Howell and Mariana Raykova published Pinocchio: Nearly Practical Verifiable Computation (IEEE S&P 2013; ePrint received 16 May 2013). It produced 288-byte proofs with about 10 ms verification, making zk-SNARKs practical.

title: BCTV14 SNARK
brief: Eli Ben-Sasson, Alessandro Chiesa, Eran Tromer and Madars Virza posted "Succinct Non-Interactive Zero Knowledge for a von Neumann Architecture" (ePrint received 30 Dec 2013; USENIX Security 2014). This BCTV14 proving system was used for Sprout, and a flaw in the paper later led to CVE-2019-7167.

title: Equihash paper
brief: Alex Biryukov and Dmitry Khovratovich posted Equihash, a memory-hard proof-of-work based on the generalized birthday problem (ePrint received 28 Sep 2015). It was accepted at NDSS 2016 and became Zcash's mining algorithm.

title: Zcash tech preview
brief: Zooko Wilcox's team released a public alpha "Technology Preview" of Zcash, a Bitcoin Core fork implementing the Zerocash protocol on a test network. The company had raised more than $715,000 from early investors including Naval Ravikant, Barry Silbert and Roger Ver.

title: Groth16
brief: Jens Groth published "On the Size of Pairing-based Non-interactive Arguments" (EUROCRYPT 2016; ePrint received 8 Mar 2016), with proofs of only 3 group elements. Groth16 replaced BCTV14 in the Sapling upgrade, which also closed the counterfeiting bug.

title: Zcash Foundation
brief: The Zcash Foundation made its first announcement, having incorporated in Delaware on 14 Feb 2017 as a nonprofit. Its bootstrap board was Andrew Miller (chair), Peter Van Valkenburgh, Matthew Green and Naval Ravikant. CoinDesk reported on 17 March an endowment of 273,000 ZEC pledged from Founders' Reward recipients.
people: Zooko Wilcox: pledged half his Founders' Reward

title: J.P. Morgan Quorum ZSL
brief: The Zerocoin Electric Coin Company announced a partnership with J.P. Morgan to add a Zero-knowledge Security Layer (ZSL) to Quorum, J.P. Morgan's enterprise blockchain. The integration and first open-source release followed on 17 Oct 2017.
people: Jack Gavigan: author of Oct 2017 release post

title: Powers of Tau paper
brief: Sean Bowe, Ariel Gabizon and Ian Miers published "Scalable Multi-party Computation for zk-SNARK Parameters in the Random Beacon Model" (ePrint received 31 Oct 2017). It removed the precommitment round, so ceremonies could scale to many participants.

title: Zcash Trust formed
brief: The Zcash Investment Trust, later Grayscale Zcash Trust (ZEC), was formed as a Delaware statutory trust and offered by private placement. Its shares were later quoted on OTCQX under ZCSH.

title: Counterfeit bug found
brief: Ariel Gabizon, a cryptographer at the Zerocoin Electric Coin Company, discovered a flaw inherited from the BCTV14 paper that could allow undetectable counterfeiting of shielded ZEC. It was kept secret until Sapling fixed it.

title: First ZF director
brief: Josh Cincinnati became the Zcash Foundation's first Executive Director, leaving Lyft to work full time from 12 March 2018. He resigned on 31 July 2020 after three years.
people: Josh Cincinnati: Executive Director, Zcash Foundation

title: Powers of Tau done
brief: The Zcash Foundation's Powers of Tau ceremony ran from November 2017 to April 2018 and accepted 87 contributions. Andrew Miller and Ryan Pierce flew with radioactive material to seed randomness, and Filippo Valsorda wrote an independent Go implementation.

title: Gemini lists ZEC
brief: Gemini announced Zcash trading and custody with NYDFS approval, calling itself the first licensed Zcash exchange in the world. That made the NYDFS the first regulator to supervise Zcash.

title: Overwinter
brief: Zcash's first network upgrade activated at 01:37 UTC, adding versioning and replay protection for future upgrades, faster transparent transaction verification, and transaction expiry. ZIPs: 143, 200, 201, 202 (v3 transactions) and 203 (expiry).

title: Zcon0 Montreal
brief: The Zcash Foundation held its first annual conference, Zcon0, on 26 to 28 June 2018 in Montreal under the theme "Privacy from A to Zcon". Developers from Ethereum, Monero, ZenCash, Siacoin and Coda attended.

title: Sapling MPC done
brief: Sean Bowe announced completion of the Sapling MPC, the circuit-specific second phase run by the Zcash Company from May to early August 2018 with over 90 contributions. ECC said the Powers of Tau and Sapling MPC were the largest multi-party computations ever performed.

title: Coinbase Pro lists ZEC
brief: Coinbase Pro began accepting ZEC deposits at 10am PT on 29 November 2018, then opened a ZEC/USDC order book. Trading was initially available in the US (excluding NY), UK, EU, Canada, Singapore and Australia.

title: CVE-2019-7167 public
brief: ECC disclosed the counterfeiting vulnerability Ariel Gabizon found on 1 March 2018 and that Sapling fixed by moving Sprout proofs to Groth16. It did not affect privacy, and ECC found no evidence it was exploited.

title: Electric Coin Co. name
brief: The "Zcash Company" (legal name Zerocoin Electric Coin Company, LLC) renamed itself the Electric Coin Company. The goal was to avoid confusion with Zcash itself and with the separate Zcash Foundation.

title: Zcon1 Split
brief: Zcon1, the Zcash Foundation's second annual conference, ran 22 to 24 June 2019 in Split, Croatia, under the theme "Zero to Privacy Hero". Its three days covered the Zcash protocol, other privacy coins and governance.

title: Blossom
brief: Blossom activated at 21:51 UTC and halved the target block time from 150 to 75 seconds, doubling throughput. The per-block reward was cut in proportion so total issuance stayed the same. ZIPs: 206 (deployment) and 208.

title: ZIP 1014 poll
brief: The Zcash Foundation published poll results approving ZIP 1014, which splits the post-Canopy 20% dev fund as ECC 35%, Zcash Foundation 25% and Major Grants 40%. 88 of 119 eligible panelists voted. ZF and ECC agreed on a Major Grant Review Committee by 14 Feb 2020.

title: FROST paper
brief: Chelsea Komlo and Ian Goldberg published FROST: Flexible Round-Optimized Schnorr Threshold Signatures (ePrint received 12 July 2020; SAC 2020). It is the basis for the Zcash Foundation's shielded multisig work.

title: Heartwood
brief: Heartwood activated around 10:56 UTC. It allowed coinbase rewards to be mined directly to shielded Sapling addresses (ZIP 213) and added Flyclient support for light clients (ZIP 221). Deployment ZIP: 250.

title: Gemini shielded
brief: Gemini became the first regulated financial institution to support ZEC withdrawals to shielded addresses, with NYDFS approval. ECC's Jack Gavigan said it showed Zcash is compatible with a robust AML/CFT regime.

title: Canopy
brief: Canopy, the fifth upgrade, activated at 12:34 UTC along with the first halving, ending the Founders' Reward. It started the ZIP 1014 dev fund (miners 80%, Major Grants 8%, ECC 7%, ZF 5%) and stopped new value entering Sprout. ZIPs: 251, 207, 211, 212, 214, 215.

title: ZOMG becomes ZCG
brief: Zcash Open Major Grants (ZOMG), the committee managing the 8% Major Grants slice, renamed itself Zcash Community Grants. It moved to zcashcommunitygrants.org and @ZcashCommGrants.

title: Halo 2 goes MIT/Apache
brief: Through an agreement with the Filecoin Foundation, ECC relicensed the Halo 2 codebase from BOSL to MIT or Apache 2.0, with a grant pool of up to $9M for Filecoin-Zcash projects. Orchard itself stayed under BOSL.

title: Zcon3 Las Vegas
brief: Zcon3 took place in Las Vegas from 7 to 9 August 2022 under the theme "Code Alone Doesn't Cut It". Speakers included Jack Gavigan, Daira Hopwood, Jack Grigg and QEDIT's Daniel Benarroch.

title: ZIP 317 fees
brief: ZIP 317 was created to replace the flat 1,000-zatoshi fee with fees proportional to transaction actions, after chain usage included 1,100-output transactions paying the same fee as 2-output ones (the "sandblasting" spam). zcashd v5.5.0 made it the default.

title: Shielded Labs
brief: Shielded Labs was founded as a donation-funded Swiss association and introduced publicly by Jason McGee on 30 Jan 2023 as an independent, non-US Zcash organization. It later drove the Crosslink hybrid PoS work and engaged Taylor Hornby for the 2026 Orchard audit.

title: Zebra 1.0
brief: The Zcash Foundation released Zebra 1.0.0, the first stable, audited version of its Rust Zcash node. It was the first Zcash node written entirely in Rust and gave the network a second independent implementation alongside zcashd.

title: Zcon4 Barcelona
brief: Zcon4 ran from 30 July to 1 August 2023 in Barcelona, Spain, under the theme "The Future Has Not Been Written". It was organized by the Zcash Foundation.

title: Zooko steps down
brief: Zooko Wilcox stepped down as CEO of Electric Coin Co., saying Zcash had taken over his identity. Josh Swihart, previously SVP of growth, became ECC's second CEO, and Zooko stayed on the Bootstrap board.

title: Binance monitoring tag
brief: Binance put ZEC, XMR, FIRO, ZEN and six other tokens under its Monitoring Tag, signaling possible delisting. Zcash responded with exchange-only address proposals (TEX and traceable UA), which DL News reported protected ZEC from immediate delisting.

title: FROST 1.0
brief: The Zcash Foundation released frost-core 1.0.0, an audited Rust reference implementation of two-round FROST threshold Schnorr signatures. It included the frost-rerandomized variant needed for unlinkable Zcash shielded multisig (ZIP 312).

title: Zashi wallet
brief: ECC launched Zashi, its own mobile Zcash wallet, on iOS, with Android to follow in late April. Version 1.0 supported Sapling and Orchard, unified addresses and "Spend before Sync".

title: Gavigan leaves ZF
brief: Jack Gavigan stepped down after four years as Zcash Foundation Executive Director, saying there was no disagreement with the board. COO Alex Bornstein became interim Executive Director.

title: Bornstein ZF director
brief: The Zcash Foundation named Alex Bornstein permanent Executive Director. It also promoted Pili Guerra to Head of Engineering and Danika Delano to COO.

title: NU6.1
brief: NU6.1 activated at 19:56 UTC with a dual funding model: 8% of block rewards to Zcash Community Grants and 12% to a fund directed by coinholder decisions. It also provided a one-time lockbox disbursement. ZIPs: 255 (deployment), 271, 1016, 214.

title: ECC team resigns
brief: The entire Electric Coin Company staff, led by CEO Josh Swihart, resigned in what he called constructive discharge after a dispute with the Bootstrap board. He named board members Zaki Manian, Christina Garman, Alan Fairless and Michelle Lai as misaligned with Zcash's mission.

title: cashZ announced
brief: Less than a day after leaving ECC, the former team announced a new Zcash startup and the cashZ wallet, built on the Zashi codebase with migration for Zashi users. Swihart said startups can scale and nonprofits cannot.

title: ZODL raises $25M
brief: Zcash Open Development Lab (ZODL), the company formed by the ex-ECC team, announced a seed round of over $25M. Backers included Paradigm, a16z crypto, Winklevoss Capital and Coinbase Ventures, and the wallet once called Zashi is now named Zodl.

title: Orchard bug found
brief: Taylor Hornby, engaged by Shielded Labs for an AI-assisted audit, found a soundness bug in the Orchard circuit's variable-base scalar multiplication. It could have allowed unlimited undetectable counterfeit ZEC and had been present since Orchard activated in May 2022. He reported it to ZODL the same day, and no evidence of exploitation was found, though none can be proven.

title: Orchard soft fork
brief: An emergency soft fork in zcashd v6.12.5 and zebra v4.5.3 banned all Orchard actions from height 3363426. An earlier attempt at 3363366 failed because some mining pools had not upgraded. It closed the vulnerability window while the fixed circuit was prepared (ZIP 257).

title: NU6.2
brief: NU6.2 was an emergency upgrade (Zebra 5.0.0) that re-enabled Orchard with a corrected scalar multiplication gadget and a new verifying key. It also enforced a canonical proof length. Deployment ZIP: 257.

title: Zcash ETF (ZCSH)
brief: Grayscale's Zcash ETF began trading on NYSE Arca under ZCSH, converted from the trust formed in October 2017. Grayscale called it the first ETP in the world offering spot ZEC exposure.
people: Steve Vanourny: Grayscale Head of Index
